newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CBANK CHECKING PRICES OF CROWN -DEALER.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CBANK CHECKING PRICES OF CROWN -DEALER.

text.p: The Czech crown fell to minus 10.0 percent against the mid-point of its former mark/dollar fixing basket on Tuesday morning prompting the Czech National Bank (CNB) to check prices on the market, a senior dealer said.

"Now the CNB was checking prices on the market...I think there is interest from between 19.2 and 20.00 (against the mark) from the CNB to defend the crown," Tomas Becvar of Komercni Banka told Reuters.

At 0640 GMT the crown was trading at 32.707 to the dollar and 19.190 to the mark implying a deviation from the old basket, which was abolished as a marker for the crown on Monday evening, of 9.56 percent.

The CNB abolished the plus/minus 7.5 percent fluctuation bands for the crown on Monday evening and also raised the discount rate to 13.0 percent from 10.5 percent after several days of sustained speculative pressure from home and abroad.
The CNB said on Monday that it anticipated turbulance on Tuesday morning, adding that it was still ready to defend the crown to keep it stable.
"We have liquid funds at our disposal exceeding $10 billion for the support of the crown," CNB open market operations director Ludek Niedermeyer said on Monday.
